content: The two pointer logic you used is totally spot on and hits that optimal O(N log N) sweet spot, which is perfect. But there are two quick Python tricks you can try. First, using input() inside a loop is notoriously slow for big test cases. If you swap to sys.stdin.read().split(), you can grab everything at once and totally avoid that massive slowdown. Second, calling the built-in max() function inside your while loop adds a tiny bit of extra work every single pass. Since the room count only goes up by 1 anyway, swapping it for a simple if rooms > max_rooms: check is actually noticeably faster when the code actually runs. Great algorithmic approach though.

This is a really fun clash! However, there's still room for improvement. After looking at 5DN1L's comment, most of the issues they pointed out are already resolved, but I still see a few remaining. One small issue I noticed is that N is not formatted as a [[variable]] in the Goal section.

My main problem is with the grouping of the test cases and validators. As 5DN1L stated, validators should be similar to their corresponding test cases, only differing slightly in inputs and outputs. For example, the current test case Exact Reuse would work well as the validator for the test case No Overlap, because both test cases involve meetings starting right as another meeting ends in a single meeting room. In fact, with the exception of Exact Reuse (as well as possibly Mixed Overlap and Unsorted Input), I believe all of the test cases and validators could work as their own test cases. This is somewhat of a personal opinion though, so it's your discretion on how the test cases and validators should be arranged.

I also think that the test cases may not be exhaustive enough, specifically missing the last three bullet points in 5DN1L's comment. However, that may result in too many test cases. Personally, the highest amount of test cases I've seen in clashes is around 10-12, so whether you're fine with that or prefer to minimize the amount of cases is your decision.

Aside from that, great work with the clash! Once the test cases are revised, this clash should be ready for approval.

Formatting / presentation
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Goal
* Please format "N" as a [[variable]].

Input
* Please format all variable names (N, start, end) as [[variables]].

* Please follow the example shown in the above-mentioned link to simplify the section:

  - Change "The first line contains an" to "<<Line 1>>: An".
  
  - Change "The next N lines each contain two" to "<<Next [[N]] lines>>: Each line contains two space-separated".

Output
* Please change "Print a" to "<<Line 1>>: A".

Constraints
* Please format all variable names (N, start, end) as [[variables]].

* Please change 10^5 to 100 as [[N]] never exceeds 10 in the current cases.

* Please change 10^9 to 100 as [[start]] and [[end]] never exceed 100 in the current cases.

Cases
* Each test and its validator should cover the same scenario, differing only slightly in inputs and outputs. Please revise the cases accordingly.

* Please rename the cases with descriptions of the scenarios they cover. Alternatively, you can reply here with a brief summary of the scenario covered by each case pair (test + validator).

* Please add a case pair that includes multiple pairs of meetings, each of which share the same start time but have different end times.

* Please add a case pair that includes multiple pairs of meetings, each of which share the same end time but have different start times.

* Please add a case pair that includes multiple pairs of meetings, each of which share the same start time and the same end time.

* Please add a case pair that combines all three of the scenarios mentioned above in a single test, with multiple overlaps.

* Please add some cases with highly randomised inputs, with [[N]] between 10 and 100.

Thanks.

5DN1L will probably show up in a minute to tell you about the formatting and the duplicated validators.
